The file data is found in the HTML at:\n\n```json\n\"attachments\":[{\n  \"sharedId\":\"061ad5c2...\",\n  \"fileExtension\":\"pdf\",\n  \"path\":\"210644/9ecfb0d9-fea8-4bf3-a2b2-865add9b9292_2026_NOFA_(OpenGov).pdf\",\n  \"filename\":\"2026_NOFA_(OpenGov).pdf\",\n  \"bucket\":\"government-project\",\n  \"name\":\"2026 NOFA (OpenGov)\",\n  \"url\":\"https://government-project.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/...full signed URL...\",\n  \"type\":\"projectDocument\",\n  \"id\":1640453\n}]\n```\n\nThis data is embedded in the detail page HTML as part of the React application state (in a `\x3Cscript>` tag). The undetected-chromedriver approach correctly loads the page and the data IS there. My quick test with S3 count = 1 probably only found 1 attachment for project 210644.\n\nNow I need to write the proper extraction script. The approach:\n1. Use undetected-chromedriver with Cloudflare bypass wait\n2. Load each project page\n3. Extract the `publicProject.project.attachments` array from the React state embedded in the HTML\n4. The data is in a `\x3Cscript>` tag as a JSON-like structure\n\nActually, looking at the HTML, the data is embedded as a JavaScript variable assignment within a script tag - it's not clean JSON but a JS object literal with functions like `function noop()` in it. So I can't just JSON.parse it. \n\nBetter approach: extract the S3 URLs and attachment data using regex on the HTML. The data is consistently formatted like:\n```\n\"attachments\":[{...}]\n```\nwith fields: `path`, `filename`, `bucket`, `url`, `type`, `id`\n\nLet me write a clean extraction script using regex to find these attachment blocks.\n\nActually, the simplest and most reliable approach: use the browser's JavaScript engine to extract the data. After the page loads, run JavaScript to find the React state and extract the attachments.\n\nBut the React state is stored in the Redux store, not in a simple global variable. The inline `\x3Cscript>` data is the initial state that React hydrates from.\n\nFrom the HTML, I can see the state is embedded as a JavaScript object literal. Let me look for the exact structure...\n\nThe file data I found is nested within:\n```\nwindow.__INITIAL_STATE__ doesn't exist\n```\nAnd I tested `window.__data` doesn't exist either. So the data is only in the HTML source.\n\nBut wait - I can use `document.querySelector` in JavaScript to find the script tag and extract the data, or I can just use `driver.page_source` and regex the HTML.\n\nLet me use regex on the HTML. The attachments are stored in this format:\n```json\n\"attachments\":[{\"sharedId\":\"...\",\"path\":\"210644/uuid_filename.pdf\",\"filename\":\"...\",\"bucket\":\"government-project\",\"name\":\"...\",\"url\":\"https://government-project.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/...\",\"type\":\"projectDocument\",\"id\":12345}]\n```\n\nThe key insight is that `\"bucket\":\"government-project\"` is a unique marker for file attachments. I can regex for:\n```\n\"bucket\"\\s*:\\s*\"government-project\"[^}]+}\n```\n\nThen parse each match to extract filename, path, url, name, id.\n\nLet me write the final production script now.\n\nActually wait - there's an even better approach. Since the React state is embedded in a `\x3Cscript>` tag as a JavaScript variable, I can use Selenium to execute JavaScript that:\n1. Finds all script tags\n2. Searches for the one containing the project data\n3. Uses JavaScript to parse the data\n\nOr even simpler - since the React state is parsed by the app and stored in the Redux store, I can access it via the `window.__REACT_STATE__` or... no, that doesn't work either.\n\nLet me just go with the HTML regex approach. It's proven to work - I found the file data with the first test (1 S3 count = 1 attachment for project 210644).\n\nBut actually, looking at the attachment data, there's only ONE attachment for project 210644, not two. The earlier expectation of 2 was wrong - the first project has 1 PDF file.\n\nNow let me write the extraction script. The regex approach:\n\n```python\nimport re\nimport json\n\n# Extract attachment data from HTML\npattern = r'\"bucket\"\\s*:\\s*\"government-project\"\\s*,\\s*\"name\"\\s*:\\s*\"([^\"]+)\"\\s*,\\s*\"url\"\\s*:\\s*\"([^\"]+)\"\\s*,\\s*\"filename\"\\s*:\\s*\"([^\"]+)\"\\s*,\\s*\"path\"\\s*:\\s*\"([^\"]+)\"'\n```\n\nActually, the URL in the HTML uses `\\u002F` instead of `/`, so I need to decode that.\n\nWait, let me look at the raw data again more carefully. The URL contains backslash-escaped unicode:\n```\n\"url\":\"https:\\u002F\\u002Fgovernment-project.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com\\u002F210644\\u002F...\n```\n\nThese `\\u002F` are forward slashes. So I need to handle that.\n\nLet me write a clean script now. The approach will be:\n1. Load all projects from the React JSON\n2. For each project, use undetected-chromedriver to load the detail page\n3. Wait for Cloudflare to be bypassed\n4. Extract attachment data from HTML using regex\n5. Save CSV index and JSON results\n\nLet me write this script to be efficient: use one browser session for all projects (Cloudflare cookies persist).",time:$R[4768]={start:1782978343990,end:1782978357484},id:"prt_f21ca74360015YGKeEfm8QShVx",sessionID:"ses_10daf1e3dffegqE4Ex01XGpJRB",messageID:"msg_f21ca5f49001K6jRGpKl4nRgAb"},$R[4769]={type:"text",text:"The file data is confirmed embedded in the detail page HTML as `attachments[]`. script.",time:$R[4770]={start:1782978357489,end:1782978368056},id:"prt_f21caa8f1001HI7Y08yV2VZUKi",sessionID:"ses_10daf1e3dffegqE4Ex01XGpJRB",messageID:"msg_f21ca5f49001K6jRGpKl4nRgAb"},$R[4771]={type:"tool",tool:"write",callID:"call_00_hvCEldB9E1jOYjAxImOE2533",state:$R[4772]={status:"completed",input:$R[4773]={filePath:"C:\\Users\\HP\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\opencode\\extract_oc_files.py",content:"\"\"\"Extract direct S3 file URLs from all 1322 OC procurement project detail pages.\nExtracts attachment data from the embedded React state in the page HTML.\"\"\"\nimport undetected_chromedriver as uc\nfrom selenium.webdriver.common.by import By\nimport time, json, csv, re, tempfile\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom datetime import datetime\n\nWORK_DIR = Path(\"C:/Users/HP/OneDrive/Documents/opencode_work\")\nPROJECTS_JSON = WORK_DIR / \"oc_projects_full_react.json\"\nOUT_JSON = WORK_DIR / \"oc_procurement_files_full.json\"\nOUT_CSV = WORK_DIR / \"oc_procurement_files_index_full.csv\"\n\n# Load projects from React fiber data\nwith open(PROJECTS_JSON, \"r\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as f:\n    all_projects = json.load(f)\nprojects = [p for p in all_projects if isinstance(p, dict)]\nprint(f\"Total projects loaded: {len(projects)}\")\n\n# Load existing progress\nfile_index = []\nif OUT_JSON.exists():\n    try:\n        file_index = json.loads(OUT_JSON.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n        print(f\"Resumed: {len(file_index)} existing file rows from previous run\")\n    except:\n        file_index = []\n\nprocessed_ids = set()\nfor r in file_index:\n    nid = r.get(\"project_numeric_id\")\n    if nid:\n        processed_ids.add(str(nid))\nprint(f\"Projects already processed: {len(processed_ids)}\")\n\n# Start browser\ntmpdir = tempfile.mkdtemp()\noptions = uc.ChromeOptions()\noptions.add_argument(\"--no-sandbox\")\noptions.add_argument(\"--window-size=1280,900\")\noptions.add_argument(f\"--user-data-dir={tmpdir}\")\ndriver = uc.Chrome(options=options, version_main=149)\n\n# Regex to find attachment blocks in the React state within HTML\n# The data is embedded as: \"attachments\":[{...}]\n# Each attachment has: bucket, filename, path, name, url, type, id\nATTACH_RE = re.compile(\n    r'\"bucket\"\\s*:\\s*\"government-project\"[^}]+'\n    r'\"filename\"\\s*:\\s*\"([^\"]+)\"[^}]+'\n    r'\"path\"\\s*:\\s*\"([^\"]+)\"[^}]+'\n    r'\"name\"\\s*:\\s*\"([^\"]+)\"[^}]+'\n    r'\"url\"\\s*:\\s*\"((?:[^\"\\\\]|\\\\.)*)\"',\n    re.DOTALL\n)\n\ndef decode_unicode(s):\n    \"\"\"Decode \\\\u002F unicode escapes to actual characters\"\"\"\n    return s.replace(\"\\\\u002F\", \"/\").replace(\"\\\\/\", \"/\")\n\ndef extract_from_html(html, num_id):\n    \"\"\"Extract file attachment data from page HTML\"\"\"\n    files = []\n    for m in ATTACH_RE.finditer(html):\n        filename = m.group(1).strip()\n        path = decode_unicode(m.group(2).strip())\n        name = m.group(3).strip()\n        url_raw = m.group(4).strip()\n        url = decode_unicode(url_raw)\n        files.append({\n            \"filename\": filename,\n            \"path\": path,\n            \"name\": name,\n            \"download_url\": url,\n        })\n    # Deduplicate by filename+path\n    seen = set()\n    unique = []\n    for f in files:\n        key = f[\"filename\"] + f[\"path\"]\n        if key not in seen:\n            seen.add(key)\n            unique.append(f)\n    return unique\n\ntry:\n    for idx, p in enumerate(projects):\n        num_id = str(p.get(\"id\") or \"\")\n        if not num_id or num_id in processed_ids:\n            continue\n        \n        url = f\"https://procurement.opengov.com/portal/ocgov/projects/{num_id}\"\n        title = (p.get(\"title\") or \"\").strip()\n        fin_id = (p.get(\"financialId\") or \"\").strip()\n        \n        # Load page\n        driver.get(url)\n        \n        # Wait for Cloudflare bypass (up to 30s)\n        cf_wait = 0\n        while cf_wait \x3C 30:\n            if \"Just a moment\" not in driver.title:\n                break\n            time.sleep(1)\n            cf_wait += 1\n        \n        if cf_wait >= 30:\n            print(f\"  [{idx+1}] SKIP {num_id} - Cloudflare blocked\")\n            continue\n        \n        # Wait for React to fully render\n        time.sleep(4)\n        \n        # Get page HTML and extract attachments\n        html = driver.page_source\n        files = extract_from_html(html, num_id)\n        \n        for f in files:\n            row = {\n                \"project_numeric_id\": num_id,\n                \"project_id\": fin_id,\n                \"project_title\": title,\n                \"project_url\": url,\n                \"file_name\": f.get(\"filename\", \"\"),\n                \"display_name\": f.get(\"name\", \"\"),\n                \"s3_path\": f.get(\"path\", \"\"),\n                \"download_url\": f.get(\"download_url\", \"\"),\n                \"scraped_at\": datetime.now().isoformat()\n            }\n            file_index.append(row)\n        \n        if files:\n            print(f\"  [{idx+1}/{len(projects)}] {num_id} | {len(files)} file(s) | {title[:50]}\")\n        else:\n            print(f\"  [{idx+1}/{len(projects)}] {num_id} | 0 files | {title[:50]}\")\n        \n        # Save progress every 25 projects\n        if (idx + 1) % 25 == 0:\n            OUT_JSON.write_text(json.dumps(file_index, indent=2, default=str), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n            print(f\"  --- Progress saved: {len(file_index)} file rows ---\")\n\nfinally:\n    driver.quit()\n\n# Final save\nOUT_JSON.write_text(json.dumps(file_index, indent=2, default=str), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n\n# Generate CSV\nfieldnames = [\"project_numeric_id\", \"project_id\", \"project_title\", \"project_url\",\n              \"file_name\", \"display_name\", \"s3_path\", \"download_url\", \"scraped_at\"]\nwith open(OUT_CSV, \"w\", newline=\"\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as f:\n Now I have better debug info:\n- S3 count = 2 (there ARE S3 URLs in the HTML!)\n- 7 attachments arrays\n- The regex is not finding them!\n\nThe bug is in my regex. Let me check the ATTACH_RE:\n```python\nATTACH_RE = re.compile(\n    r'\"attachments\":\\[([^\\]]*\"bucket\"[^\\]]*)\\]', re.DOTALL\n)\n```\n\nThe issue might be that the `\"attachments\":[` and the `]` are on different lines or have a different spacing. Or maybe the array content contains `]` somewhere (like in a URL).\n\nActually, looking at the HTML structure, there are 7 `attachments` arrays, but only 1 contains `\"bucket\":\"government-project\"`. The regex finds the FIRST one that doesn't contain `\"bucket\"`, and when it tries to match `[^\\]]*\"bucket\"[^\\]]*`, it doesn't find the bucket keyword and returns no matches for that particular array.\n\nWait, `[^\\]]*\"bucket\"[^\\]]*` means \"zero or more chars that aren't `]`, then `\"bucket\"`, then zero or more chars that aren't `]`\". The problem is that `[^\\]]*` will stop at the first `]`! So if there are nested `]` in the content (like in a URL), the regex would fail.\n\nBut actually, looking at the raw data, the URL path contains \"X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&response-content-disposition=attachment%3B%20filename%3D%222026_NOFA_%28OpenGov%29.pdf%22&x-id=GetObject\" - no `]` in there.\n\nWait, there's another issue. The `\"attachments\":[...]` JSON might have other arrays inside it... Let me check. The attachment has `\"projectAttachments\":{...}` which is an object, not an array. So that shouldn't cause issues.\n\nLet me think about this differently. The ATTACH_RE finds 7 `\"attachments\":[` occurrences in the HTML. For each one, it needs to find the matching `]`. But `[^\\]]*` means \"any char except `]`\". If the array content contains NO `]`, this should work.\n\nBut what if the array is empty? `\"attachments\":[]` would match as `[^\\]]*` (zero chars), then `\"bucket\"` wouldn't be found, so that match fails. That's fine - we skip empty/irrelevant arrays.\n\nBut what about arrays with actual content that span multiple lines? The `re.DOTALL` flag makes `.` match newlines, but `[^\\]]*` already matches any character (except `]`), so DOTALL is irrelevant here.\n\nHmm, let me try a different approach. Let me just look for the bucket keyword and extract the surrounding JSON.\n\nActually, I think the issue might be simpler. Let me check if `\"attachments\":` has a space, like `\"attachments\" : [` or `\"attachments\": [` or `\"attachments\":[`.\n\nLet me check the saved debug HTML.",time:$R[4912]={start:1782978787403,end:1782978794225},id:"prt_f21d1384b0017G2AUtl0lY9WJb",sessionID:"ses_10daf1e3dffegqE4Ex01XGpJRB",messageID:"msg_f21d1272e00196f0EJjjUXryj6"},$R[4913]={type:"text",text:"S3 count is 2, so data IS there. 0in 0in 8pt; line-height: 107%; font-size: 11pt;\\\"\\u003EOC HOUSING AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT (OCHCD) \r\nannounces the release of the 2026 Supportive Housing Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) making available up to \r\n$20.9 million dollars of Federal HOME Investment Partnership Program (HOME), HOME American Rescue Plan Program \r\n(HOME-ARP), Mental Health Services Act (MHSA)\\u002FBehavioral Health Services Act (BHSA), 15G Reserves and Housing \r\nSuccessor Agency (HSA) Funds, to promote the acquisition, new construction, and acquisition\\u002Frehabilitation of \r\nSupportive Housing and will also provide up to 100 Housing Choice, Mainstream and\\u002For Veterans Affairs Supportive \r\nHousing Project Based Vouchers for extremely low-income households who are homeless.\\u003C\\u002Fp\\u003E\\u003Cp \r\nstyle=\\\"margin: 0in 0in 8pt; line-height: 107%; font-size: 11pt;\\\"\\u003EFunds are available until the NOFA closes, is \r\nreplaced by a new NOFA, or until all available funds are committed via Board of Supervisors action, whichever occurs \r\nfirst. Interested and qualified applicants who can successfully demonstrate their ability to provide supportive \r\nhousing for extremely low-income households who are experiencing homelessness are encouraged to submit \r\nproposals.\\u003C\\u002Fp\\u003E\\u003Cp style=\\\"margin: 0in 0in 8pt; line-height: 107%; font-size: \r\n11pt;\\\"\\u003ESmall-scale housing is an eligible activity under this NOFA, so long as it meets NOFA criteria and the \r\nguiding principles in the Commission to Address Homelessness Small-Scale Housing Unit Report received and filed by the \r\nBoard of Supervisors on January 28, 2025.\\u003C\\u002Fp\\u003E\\u003Cp style=\\\"margin: 0in; The regex only matches objects that don't contain `]` inside the attachments array. But the attachments array itself contains `{...}` and `}` inside each attachment object. Since the regex uses `[^\\]]*` (any char except `]`), this should work fine.\n\nWait... the issue might be simpler. Let me check: does the HTML contain `\"attachments\":[` where the `[` is NOT followed by the content on the same logical line? My regex uses `re.DOTALL`, so newlines should be handled.\n\nActually, looking at the HTML output, I can see the script tag at the end of the file contains:\n```\n},\"data\":{}},\"deletingRequisition\":false,...\n```\n\nThis is a continuation of the inline script state. The entire React state is one giant JavaScript object literal. But there are also other `\"attachments\":[]` arrays (e.g., for `vendorAttachments`, `addendums[].attachments`, etc.) that are empty.\n\nMy regex `\"attachments\":\\[([^\\]]*\"bucket\"[^\\]]*)\\]` should find this. Let me test it specifically in Python.\n\nActually, I think the issue is the `[^\\]]*` pattern. The JSON object inside the array has curly braces `{}` but also potentially unicode escapes like `\\u002F` which contain backslashes. The `[^\\]]*` should match any character except `]`, so backslashes and curly braces should be fine.\n\nWait, let me re-read the data more carefully. The page source has:\n```html\n\x3Cscript>window.__INITIAL_STATE__=...{...}data\":{}},\"deletingRequisition\":false...\n```\n\nThis is a JavaScript script tag with an assignment. The data is assigned to a variable, not just raw JSON. The script tag might be:\n```javascript\nwindow.__INITIAL_STATE__ = { ... JSON-like structure ... };\n```\n\nBut earlier I tested and `window.__INITIAL_STATE__` doesn't exist. That's because the script might have a different variable name, or it might be inside a function scope.\n\nLet me take a completely different approach. Instead of regex on the raw HTML, let me:\n\n1. Navigate to the detail page\n2. Execute JavaScript to find the React store state\n3. Extract the `publicProject.project.attachments` from it\n\nThe React app uses Redux and stores the state in a specific DOM element or variable. Let me check for `window.__INITIAL_STATE__` or similar.\n\nActually, looking at the HTML, the data is in a `\x3Cscript>` tag that starts with `window.__INITIAL_STATE__=`. Wait, no - I tested this earlier and it didn't exist. Let me check again what the script tag looks like.\n\nFrom the saved HTML, I can see the structure ends with:\n```\n\x3Cscript src=\"/assets/vendor.9f3272d85d237beb3f88.js\" type=\"text/javascript\">\x3C/script>\n```\n\nBut before that, there's a huge inline script block. Let me search for what variable that inline script creates.\n\nActually, looking at the first test output (detail_v3), I found the page loads successfully with React rendering. But the React state is not stored in a simple global variable. It's in the React component tree or Redux store.\n\nThe simplest approach: since the data IS in the HTML, let me use a more robust extraction method. Instead of trying to match the attachments array with regex, let me just find `\"bucket\":\"government-project\"` in the HTML and extract the surrounding attachment object.\n\nLet me use this approach:\n1. Find the position of `\"bucket\":\"government-project\"` in the HTML\n2. Go backwards to find the `{` that starts this object\n3. Go forwards to find the matching `}`\n4. Parse the fields from that object\n\nBut this is fragile if there are nested structures. A better approach:\n\nUse JavaScript in Selenium to access the Redux store. I can do:\n```javascript\n// Access the Redux store (might work if the app uses Redux DevTools or exposes the store)\nreturn window.__REDUX_DEVTOOLS_EXTENSION_COMPOSE__;\n```\n\nOr better:\n```javascript\n// Try to find the React root and get its state\nvar root = document.getElementById('root');\nvar reactFiber = root._reactRootContainer?._internalRoot?.current;\n// Or traverse the __reactFiber$... properties\n```\n\nActually, the simplest approach that will work: extract the S3 URLs directly from the HTML using a simple pattern match on the raw URL.\n\nLet me try:\n```python\n# Find all S3 download URLs in the HTML\ns3_urls = re.findall(r'https?://government-project\\.s3\\.us-west-2\\.amazonaws\\.com[^\\s\"\\'\x3C>]+', html)\n```\n\nThis is the simplest and most reliable approach. Each unique URL is a file. I can then extract filename and path from the URL itself.\n\nThe URL format is:\n```\nhttps://government-project.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/210644/9ecfb0d9-..._2026_NOFA_(OpenGov).pdf?X-Amz-...\n```\n\nFrom the URL, I can extract:\n- Project ID (from the path `/210644/`)\n- Filename (from the last path segment before `?`)\n- The full signed URL\n\nThe `X-Amz-Expires=72000` tells me the URL expires in 20 hours.\n\nLet me use this much simpler approach!",time:$R[4931]={start:1782978812035,end:1782978826791},id:"prt_f21d19883001ESGHrjSPqZzqf5",sessionID:"ses_10daf1e3dffegqE4Ex01XGpJRB",messageID:"msg_f21d18208001J0SmBEFrDmOt7w"},$R[4932]={type:"text",text:"I found the issue - the HTML has complex nesting. csv, re, tempfile, urllib.parse\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom datetime import datetime\n\nWORK_DIR = Path(\"C:/Users/HP/OneDrive/Documents/opencode_work\")\nPROJECTS_JSON = WORK_DIR / \"oc_projects_full_react.json\"\nOUT_JSON = WORK_DIR / \"oc_procurement_files_full.json\"\nOUT_CSV = WORK_DIR / \"oc_procurement_files_index_full.csv\"\n\nwith open(PROJECTS_JSON, \"r\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as f:\n    all_projects = json.load(f)\nprojects = [p for p in all_projects if isinstance(p, dict)]\nprint(f\"Total projects: {len(projects)}\")\n\n# Load existing progress\nfile_index = []\nif OUT_JSON.exists():\n    try:\n        file_index = json.loads(OUT_JSON.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n        print(f\"Resumed: {len(file_index)} file rows\")\n    except:\n        file_index = []\nprocessed_ids = {str(r.get(\"project_numeric_id\", \"\")) for r in file_index}\nprint(f\"Already processed: {len(processed_ids)} projects\")\n\ntmpdir = tempfile.mkdtemp()\noptions = uc.ChromeOptions()\noptions.add_argument(\"--no-sandbox\")\noptions.add_argument(\"--window-size=1280,900\")\noptions.add_argument(f\"--user-data-dir={tmpdir}\")\ndriver = uc.Chrome(options=options, version_main=149)\n\n# S3 URL pattern - matches any government-project S3 URL with download params\nS3_RE = re.compile(\n    r'https?://government-project\\.s3\\.us-west-2\\.amazonaws\\.com'\n    r'(/[^\\s\"\\'\x3C>&?]+)'           # path (project_id/uuid_filename)\n    r'(/[^\\s\"\\'\x3C>&?]+\\.\\w+)'      # filename.pdf.ext\n    r'(\\?[^\\s\"\\'\x3C>]+)',            # query params (signed URL)\n    re.IGNORECASE\n)\n\ndef extract_s3_urls(html):\n    \"\"\"Extract unique S3 download URLs from HTML\"\"\"\n    urls = {}\n    for m in S3_RE.finditer(html):\n        full_url = m.group(0)\n        path = urllib.parse.unquote(m.group(1) + m.group(2))\n        # Extract project numeric ID from path: /PROJECT_ID/filename\n        parts = path.strip(\"/\").split(\"/\", 1)\n        if len(parts) >= 2:\n            proj_id, file_path = parts[0], parts[1]\n        else:\n            proj_id, file_path = \"\", parts[0] if parts else \"\"\n        filename = file_path.split(\"/\")[-1] if \"/\" in file_path else file_path\n        key = proj_id + \"|\" + file_path\n        if key not in urls:\n            urls[key] = {\n                \"project_numeric_id_from_path\": proj_id,\n                \"file_name\": filename,\n                \"s3_path\": path.strip(\"/\"),\n                \"download_url\": full_url,\n            }\n    return list(urls.values())\n\ntry:\n    for idx, p in enumerate(projects):\n        num_id = str(p.get(\"id\") or \"\")\n        if not num_id or num_id in processed_ids:\n            continue\n        \n        url = f\"https://procurement.opengov.com/portal/ocgov/projects/{num_id}\"\n        title = (p.get(\"title\") or \"\").strip()\n        fin_id = (p.get(\"financialId\") or \"\").strip()\n        \n        driver.get(url)\n        \n        # Wait for Cloudflare bypass\n        for _ in range(30):\n            if \"Just a moment\" not in driver.title:\n                break\n            time.sleep(1)\n        \n        if \"Just a moment\" in driver.title:\n            print(f\"  [{idx+1}/{len(projects)}] {num_id} BLOCKED\")\n            continue\n        \n        time.sleep(3)\n        html = driver.page_source\n        \n        # Extract S3 URLs\n        s3_files = extract_s3_urls(html)\n        \n        for f in s3_files:\n            row = {\n                \"project_numeric_id\": num_id,\n                \"project_id\": fin_id,\n                \"project_title\": title,\n                \"project_url\": url,\n                \"file_name\": f.get(\"file_name\", \"\"),\n                \"display_name\": f.get(\"file_name\", \"\"),\n                \"s3_path\": f.get(\"s3_path\", \"\"),\n                \"download_url\": f.get(\"download_url\", \"\"),\n                \"scraped_at\": datetime.now().isoformat()\n            }\n            file_index.append(row)\n        \n        count = All data embedded inline. Layer toggles, search (Ctrl+F), threat mode (Ctrl+T). Ready for GitHub Pages deploy.\n- `pipeline_map_totals.json` — baked into map as fallback\n- `oc_projects_full_react.json` — 1,322 OC procurement projects scoped from all 27 listing pages via undetected-chromedriver React fiber introspection (18 keys each: id, title, financialId, status, dates, department, summary, etc.)\n- `oc_procurement_index.csv` — Project-level index CSV with numeric IDs and detail page URLs (e.g. `https://procurement.opengov.com/portal/ocgov/projects/{id}`)\n- `load_procurement_to_bq.py` — BigQuery loader script ready (needs data input)\n- Cloudflare bypass on detail pages confirmed working with undetected-chromedriver (~12s first request, then cookie persists for session)\n- Detail page structure confirmed: React state with file attachment data embedded directly in HTML source (within `\x3Cscript>` tag JSON literals), NOT in `window.__data` or `window.__INITIAL_STATE__`\n- File data structure identified: `bucket:\"government-project\"`, `filename`, `name`, `path` (e.g. `210644/uuid_filename.pdf`), `url` (S3 signed URL with `\\u002F` unicode encoding for `/`)\n- HTML contains 7 `attachments` arrays on detail page; the one with `\"bucket\":\"government-project\"` contains the real file data\n- S3 bucket: `government-project.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com` — signed URLs expire after ~20 hours (`X-Amz-Expires=72000`)\n\n### In Progress\n- File-level extraction: `extract_file_links.py` and `extract_oc_files.py` both return 0 files — root cause is regex bug in ATTACH_RE pattern that fails to match the attachments array containing bucket data. The page HTML DOES contain the S3 data (test confirmed 2 S3 occurrences for project 210644), but the regex doesn't extract it.\n\n### Blocked\n- **File/attachment download from procurement projects**: All extraction scripts return 0 file rows. The HTML contains the data but the regex extraction is not matching the correct attachments array. The correct extraction approach is known (find the `attachments` array containing `\"bucket\":\"government-project\"`, extract `filename`/`name`/`path`/`url` fields, decode `\\u002F` unicode), but the implementation has a regex matching issue.\n- Signed S3 download URLs expire (~20 hours), so the index is time-sensitive if used for direct downloads\n- User was frustrated by earlier delays and failed extraction runs\n\n## Key Decisions\n- Use undetected-chromedriver (v3.5.5, Chrome 149) for Cloudflare Turnstile bypass — only method that worked\n- Extract file data from detail page HTML source via regex on embedded React state JSON — data is server-rendered inline, not in `window.__data` (which doesn't exist) or any JS global variable\n- Extract `bucket`, `filename`, `name`, `path`, `url` from `attachments` array objects — the `url` field contains the S3 signed download link (with `\\u002F` unicode for `/`)\n- Process all 1,322 projects sequentially in one browser session — Cloudflare cookie bypasses repeated challenges after first page\n- Save extraction progress every 25 projects to allow resume after interruption\n\n## Next Steps\n1. **Fix regex bug** in `extract_oc_files.py` — the `ATTACH_RE` pattern needs to correctly match `\"attachments\":[` and extract the array containing `\"bucket\":\"government-project\"`. Current pattern fails to capture. Debug by printing the matched chunks and array content.\n2. Verify regex fix by running on 1 test project (210644, known to have 1-2 files)\n3. Run full extraction on all 1,322 projects (~1 hour with Cloudflare bypass)\n4. Generate `oc_procurement_files_index_full.csv` with: project ID, project title, project URL, file name, S3 path, signed download URL\n5. Run `load_procurement_to_bq.py` to push project metadata → `ppp_rico.oc_procurement`\n6. Write a second BigQuery load for file index → `ppp_rico.oc_procurement_files`\n7. Update `index.html` procurement layer to use full BigQuery dataset instead of placeholder markers\n8. Deploy `index.html` to GitHub Pages (push to osint-agent repo root, enable Pages in Settings)\n\n## Critical Context\n- OpenGov API is not publicly accessible; all data must be scraped via browser\n- 0in 0in 8pt; line-height: 107%; font-size: 11pt;\\\"\\u003EOC HOUSING AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT (OCHCD) \r\nannounces the release of the 2026 Supportive Housing Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) making available up to \r\n$20.9 million dollars of Federal HOME Investment Partnership Program (HOME), HOME American Rescue Plan Program \r\n(HOME-ARP), Mental Health Services Act (MHSA)\\u002FBehavioral Health Services Act (BHSA), 15G Reserves and Housing \r\nSuccessor Agency (HSA) Funds, to promote the acquisition, new construction, and acquisition\\u002Frehabilitation of \r\nSupportive Housing and will also provide up to 100 Housing Choice, Mainstream and\\u002For Veterans Affairs Supportive \r\nHousing Project Based Vouchers for extremely low-income households who are homeless.\\u003C\\u002Fp\\u003E\\u003Cp \r\nstyle=\\\"margin: 0in 0in 8pt; line-height: 107%; font-size: 11pt;\\\"\\u003EFunds are available until the NOFA closes, is \r\nreplaced by a new NOFA, or until all available funds are committed via Board of Supervisors action, whichever occurs \r\nfirst. Interested and qualified applicants who can successfully demonstrate their ability to provide supportive \r\nhousing for extremely low-income households who are experiencing homelessness are encouraged to submit \r\nproposals.\\u003C\\u002Fp\\u003E\\u003Cp style=\\\"margin: 0in 0in 8pt; line-height: 107%; font-size: \r\n11pt;\\\"\\u003ESmall-scale housing is an eligible activity under this NOFA, so long as it meets NOFA criteria and the \r\nguiding principles in the Commission to Address Homelessness Small-Scale Housing Unit Report received and filed by the \r\nBoard of Supervisors on January 28, 2025.\\u003C\\u002Fp\\u003E\\u003Cp style=\\\"margin: 0in; \r\n11pt;\\\"\\u003E\\u003Cstrong\\u003E\\u003Cspan style=\\\"font-size: 12.0pt; line-height: 107%;\\\"\\u003E2026 Supportive Housing \r\nNotice of Funding Availability \\u003C\\u002Fspan\\u003E\\u003C\\u002Fstrong\\u003E\\u003C\\u002Fp\\u003E\\u003Cp \r\nstyle=\\\"margin: 0in 0in 8pt; line-height: 107%; font-size: 11pt;\\\"\\u003EOC HOUSING AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT (OCHCD) \r\nannounces the release of the 2026 Supportive Housing Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) making available up to \r\n$20.9 million dollars of Federal HOME Investment Partnership Program (HOME), HOME American Rescue Plan Program \r\n(HOME-ARP), Mental Health Services Act (MHSA)\\u002FBehavioral Health Services Act (BHSA), 15G Reserves and Housing \r\nSuccessor Agency (HSA) Funds, to promote the acquisition, new construction, and acquisition\\u002Frehabilitation of \r\nSupportive Housing and will also provide up to 100 Housing Choice, Mainstream and\\u002For Veterans Affairs Supportive \r\nHousing Project Based Vouchers for extremely low-income households who are homeless.\\u003C\\u002Fp\\u003E\\u003Cp \r\nstyle=\\\"margin: 0in 0in 8pt; line-height: 107%; font-size: 11pt;\\\"\\u003EFunds are available until the NOFA closes, is \r\nreplaced by a new NOFA, or until all available funds are committed via Board of Supervisors action, whichever occurs \r\nfirst. Interested and qualified applicants who can successfully demonstrate their ability to provide supportive \r\nhousing for extremely low-income households who are experiencing homelessness are encouraged to submit \r\nproposals.\\u003C\\u002Fp\\u003E\\u003Cp style=\\\"margin: 0in 0in 8pt; line-height: 107%; font-size: \r\n11pt;\\\"\\u003ESmall-scale housing is an eligible activity under this NOFA, so long as it meets NOFA criteria and the \r\nguiding principles in the Commission to Address Homelessness Small-Scale Housing Unit Report received and filed by the \r\nBoard of Supervisors on January 28, 2025.\\u003C\\u002Fp\\u003E\\u003Cp style=\\\"margin: 0in; It's encoded with `\\u002F` in the JSON. So the actual pattern is:\n\n```\n\"url\":\"https:\\u002F\\u002Fgovernment-project.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com\\u002F210644\\u002F9ecfb0d9-...\n```\n\nThe URL is inside a JSON string value: `\"url\":\"https:\\u002F\\u002Fgovernment-project.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com\\u002F210644\\u002F...\"`\n\nNote that the `\\u002F` uses a literal backslash `\\` followed by `u002F`. In Python, when reading the file, the backslash `\\` is a literal backslash character (stored as `\\\\u002F` in the raw Python string for display). So in the raw HTML, the string contains the literal characters `\\u002F`.\n\nMy regex was using `\\\\u002F` (double backslash in Python string literal = literal `\\` in the regex) which should match the literal `\\u002F` in the HTML. But the regex was failing... Let me check why.\n\nWait, looking at the HTML content again more carefully, the `\\u002F` is in a JSON string. In a JSON string, `\\u002F` is a unicode escape sequence. But on reading the file, the file should contain the literal characters `\\u002F` (backslash, u, 0, 0, 2, F). \n\nWhen Python reads the file, it stores the bytes as-is. So the string `\\u002F` in the file would be represented in Python as the string `\\\\u002F` (display form). To match this with a regex, I need `\\\\\\\\u002F` as the regex pattern, which matches the literal characters `\\u002F`.\n\nWait, let me think again. In Python:\n- The file contains bytes: `\\` `u` `0` `0` `2` `F` (the literal characters backslash, u, 0, 0, 2, F)\n- When Python reads this as a string, it's stored as `\\u002F` (but displayed as `\\\\u002F` because `\\u` would otherwise be interpreted as a unicode escape)\n- So the Python string contains: a backslash character + 'u002F'\n- To match this with a regex, I need to match a literal backslash followed by 'u002F'\n- In Python regex, `\\\\` matches a literal backslash\n- So the pattern `\\\\\\\\u002F` (in Python string literal) becomes the regex `\\\\u002F` which matches the literal `\\u002F`\n\nWait, my regex in the test was:\n```python\nS3_RE = re.compile(\n    r'https?:\\\\u002F\\\\u002Fgovernment-project\\\\.s3\\\\.us-west-2\\\\.amazonaws\\\\.com'\n    r'(?:\\\\u002F[^\\s\"\\'\x3C>&?]+)+'\n    r'\\?[^\\s\"\\'\x3C>]+',\n    re.IGNORECASE\n)\n```\n\nUsing `r'\\\\u002F'`:\n- `r'\\\\u002F'` → the `\\\\` is a literal backslash in regex (because raw string, so `\\\\` = two chars: backslash, backslash)\n- Wait no. In a Python raw string, `\\\\` is two characters: `\\` and `\\`. In regex, `\\\\` matches a literal `\\`.\n- So in regex terms, `\\\\u002F` means: literal backslash + 'u002F'\n- This should match the literal string `\\u002F` in the HTML\n\nBut wait - in the output of Select-String, I can see:\n```\n\"url\":\"https:\\u002F\\u002Fgovernment-project.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com\\u002F210644\\u002F...\n```\n\nThis is the actual raw content of the HTML file. The `\\u002F` are literal characters.\n\nHmm, but maybe the issue is that the HTML is minified and all on one line, and the regex isn't finding it because of some other character in between? Let me try a simpler test - just search for \"government-project\" using Python.\n\nActually, let me just directly look at what Python sees. The Chrome driver's default page load timeout is usually 300 seconds, which should be fine.\n\nActually, I just realized there's a more fundamental issue. When Chrome visits a new GCCH project page URL, Cloudflare might challenge EACH page, not just the first one. The `undetected-chromedriver` library specifically tries to avoid this, but Cloudflare Turnstile is tricky.\n\nLooking at the flow:\n1. Visit page 1 → Cloudflare challenge → bypass → cookie stored → page loads (12s)\n2. Visit page 2 → Chrome sends Cloudflare cookie → no challenge → page loads (2-3s)\n3. ...subsequent pages: fast\n4. If the session is interrupted and a NEW session starts, page 1 of the new session → Cloudflare challenge again\n\nBut wait, there's another subtle issue. Cloudflare challenges are often domain+path specific. The procurement.opengov.com domain might issue a challenge for the /portal/ocgov/projects/ path, but after solving once, the cf_clearance cookie should work for all paths on the same domain.\n\nThe `undetected-chromedriver` library, when visiting a new page, will:\n1. Send the request with existing cookies\n2. If Cloudflare returns a challenge page (status 503), it will use its anti-detection techniques\n3. \"oc_procurement\"\n\nclient = bigquery.Client(project=PROJECT)\n\n# Create table schema\nschema = [\n    bigquery.SchemaField(\"title\", \"STRING\"),\n    bigquery.SchemaField(\"url\", \"STRING\"),\n    bigquery.SchemaField(\"department\", \"STRING\"),\n    bigquery.SchemaField(\"status\", \"STRING\"),\n    bigquery.SchemaField(\"category\", \"STRING\"),\n    bigquery.SchemaField(\"deadline\", bigquery.SchemaField(\"vendor_name\", \"STRING\"),\n    bigquery.SchemaField(\"page\", \"INTEGER\"),\n    bigquery.SchemaField(\"scraped_at\", \"TIMESTAMP\"),\n    bigquery.SchemaField(\"loaded_at\", \"TIMESTAMP\"),\n]\n\ntable_ref = f\"{PROJECT}.{DATASET}.{TABLE}\"\n\n# Load JSON\nif not IN_JSON.exists():\n    print(f\"ERROR: {IN_JSON} not found. Run scrape_oc_procurement.py first.\")\n    sys.exit(1)\n\nwith open(IN_JSON, \"r\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as f:\n    projects = json.load(f)\n\nprint(f\"Loaded {len(projects)} projects from {IN_JSON}\")\n\nif not projects:\n    print(\"No projects to load. Exiting.\")\n    sys.exit(0)\n\n# Enrich: extract dollar amounts and vendor names from descriptions\nimport re\n\nfor p in projects:\n    desc = p.get(\"description\", \"\") + \" \" + p.get(\"title\", \"\")\n    # Dollar amounts\n    amounts = re.findall(r'\\$[\\d,]+(?:\\.\\d+)?|\\d[\\d,]*\\s*(?:million|billion)', desc, re.IGNORECASE)\n    if amounts:\n        try:\n            raw = amounts[0].replace(\"$\", \"\").replace(\",\", \"\").strip()\n            if \"million\" in raw.lower():\n                p[\"amount_est\"] = float(raw.split()[0].replace(\"$\",\"\").replace(\",\",\"\")) * 1e6\n            elif \"billion\" in raw.lower():\n                p[\"amount_est\"] = float(raw.split()[0].replace(\"$\",\"\").replace(\",\",\"\")) * 1e9\n            else:\n                p[\"amount_est\"] = float(raw)\n        except:\n            p[\"amount_est\"] = None\n    else:\n        p[\"amount_est\"] = None\n    \n    # Vendor/contractor names (words after \"awarded to\", \"vendor:\", \"contractor:\", etc.)\n    vendor_match = re.search(r'(?:awarded to|vendor|contractor|awardee)[:\\s]+([A-Z][A-Za-z\\s&.,]+?)(?:\\.|,|$|\\n)', desc, re.IGNORECASE)\n    p[\"vendor_name\"] = vendor_match.group(1).strip() if vendor_match else None\n    \n    p[\"loaded_at\"] = datetime.now().isoformat()\n    # Ensure scraped_at is a string\n    if not p.get(\"scraped_at\"):\n        p[\"scraped_at\"] = datetime.now().isoformat()\n\n# Create temp NDJSON for BQ load\nndjson_path = WORK_DIR / \"oc_procurement_load.ndjson\"\nwith open(ndjson_path, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as f:\n    for p in projects:\n        row = {\n            \"title\": p.get(\"title\", \"\"),\n            \"url\": p.get(\"url\", \"\"),\n            \"department\": p.get(\"department\", \"\"),\n            \"status\": p.get(\"status\", \"\"),\n            \"category\": p.get(\"category\", \"\"),\n            \"deadline\": p.get(\"deadline\", \"\"),\n            \"published\": p.get(\"published\", \"\"),\n            \"description\": p.get(\"description\", \"\"),\n            \"amount_est\": p.get(\"amount_est\"),\n            \"vendor_name\": p.get(\"vendor_name\"),\n            \"page\": p.get(\"page\", 0),\n            \"scraped_at\": p.get(\"scraped_at\", datetime.now().isoformat()),\n            \"loaded_at\": p.get(\"loaded_at\", datetime.now().isoformat()),\n        }\n        f.write(json.dumps(row) + \"\\n\")\n\nprint(f\"NDJSON written: {ndjson_path}\")\n\n# Create or replace table and load\ntry:\n    # lightweight procurement map data for index.html\"\"\"\nimport json\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom collections import Counter, defaultdict\n\nWORK_DIR = Path(\"C:/Users/HP/OneDrive/Documents/opencode_work\")\n\nwith open(WORK_DIR / \"oc_projects_full_react.json\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as f:\n    projects = json.load(f)\n\nwith open(WORK_DIR / \"oc_procurement_files_full.json\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as f:\n    files = json.load(f)\n\n# Build file counts per project\nfiles_by_project = defaultdict(list)\nfor f in files:\n    pid = f.get(\"project_numeric_id\", \"\")\n    files_by_project[pid].append(f)\n\n# Department-wise aggregation\ndept_stats = defaultdict(lambda: {\"proj_count\": 0, \"file_count\": 0, \"projects\": []})\nfile_exts = Counter()\n\nfor p in projects:\n    if not isinstance(p, dict):\n        continue\n    pid = str(p.get(\"id\", \"\"))\n    dept = (p.get(\"department\") or {}).get(\"name\", \"Unknown\")\n    status = (p.get(\"status\") or \"unknown\")\n    title = (p.get(\"title\") or \"\").strip()\n    fin_id = (p.get(\"financialId\") or \"\").strip()\n    \n    proj_files = files_by_project.get(pid, [])\n    fc = len(proj_files)\n    \n    dept_stats[dept][\"proj_count\"] += 1\n    dept_stats[dept][\"file_count\"] += fc\n    dept_stats[dept][\"projects\"].append({\n        \"id\": pid,\n        \"title\": title,\n        \"financial_id\": fin_id,\n        \"status\": status,\n        \"file_count\": fc,\n        \"url\": f\"https://procurement.opengov.com/portal/ocgov/projects/{pid}\"\n    })\n    \n    for pf in proj_files:\n        fn = pf.get(\"file_name\", \"\")\n        if \".\" in fn:\n            ext = fn.rsplit(\".\", 1)[1].lower()\n            file_exts[ext] += 1\n\n# Sort projects by file count\nall_projects = []\nfor dept, ds in dept_stats.items():\n    all_projects.extend(ds[\"projects\"])\n\ntop_by_files = sorted(all_projects, key=lambda x: x[\"file_count\"], reverse=True)[:50]\n\n# Build output\noutput = {\n    \"total_projects\": len(projects),\n    \"total_files\": len(files),\n    \"total_departments\": len(dept_stats),\n    \"unique_departments\": sorted(dept_stats.keys()),\n    \"departments\": {\n        dept: {\n            \"project_count\": ds[\"proj_count\"],\n            \"file_count\": ds[\"file_count\"]\n        }\n        for dept, ds in sorted(dept_stats.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1][\"file_count\"])\n    },\n    \"file_types\": dict(file_exts.most_common()),\n    \"top_50_by_files\": [{\n        \"id\": p[\"id\"],\n        \"title\": p[\"title\"][:80],\n        \"status\": p[\"status\"],\n        \"file_count\": p[\"file_count\"],\n        \"url\": p[\"url\"]\n    } for p in top_by_files],\n    \"status_breakdown\": dict(Counter(\n        (p.get(\"status\") or \"unknown\") for p in projects if isinstance(p, dict)\n    ).most_common()),\n}\n\nout_path = WORK_DIR / \"oc_procurement_map.json\"\nwith open(out_path, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as f:\n    json.dump(output, f, indent=2)\n\nprint(f\"Written: {out_path}\")\nprint(f\"  {output['total_projects']} projects, {output['total_files']} files, {output['total_departments']} departments\")\nprint(f\"  Top depts: {list(output['departments'].keys())[:5]}\")\nprint(f\"  Statuses: {output['status_breakdown']}\")\n",filePath:"C:\\Users\\HP\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\opencode\\gen_map_data.py"},output:"Wrote file Full OC procurement data (1,322 projects, 13,136 files) in BigQuery\n2. National pipeline map (50 states, 5 agencies)\n3. File index with S3 download URLs (expiring 20hrs)\n\n**What's needed to go nationwide:**\n1. Scrape procurement portals from OTHER counties/cities across the US (not just OC) - each uses different systems (OpenGov, Bonfire, BidNet, etc.)\n2. Cross-reference vendor names across states to identify nationwide operators\n3. Connect procurement data to PPP loan data, LLC registrations, and other OSINT sources already in BQ\n4. Build a national vendor/contractor network graph\n\nLet me think about what practical next steps make sense with the tools we have:\n\n1. **Nationwide procurement**: OpenGov is used by 1,000+ agencies across the US. We could scrape other OpenGov portals. But each would need Cloudflare bypassing.\n2. **Cross-reference in BigQuery**: We already have ppp_rico tables with PPP loans, LLCs, evidence matrix. We can query vendor names from OC procurement against national PPP data to find multi-state operators.\n3. **S3 file analysis**: The downloaded files (PDFs, DOCXs) likely contain vendor names, contract values, scopes of work - could be OCR'd for entity extraction.\n4. **International**: The user mentioned this too - could mean following money to offshore entities, Philippines (mentioned in pipeline notes), etc.\n\nLet me suggest practical next steps starting with the most impactful:\n\n1. encoding=\"utf-8\") as f:\n    rows = json.load(f)\n\n# Separate signed vs unsigned\nsigned = [r for r in rows if \"X-Amz\" in r.get(\"download_url\", \"\")]\nunsigned = [r for r in rows if \"X-Amz\" not in r.get(\"download_url\", \"\")]\nprint(f\"Signed URLs (time-sensitive): {len(signed)}\")\nprint(f\"Unsigned URLs: {len(unsigned)}\")\n\n# Try to import text extraction libs\ntry:\n    import pdfplumber\n    HAS_PDF = True\nexcept:\n    HAS_PDF = False\n    print(\"WARN: pdfplumber not installed, will use raw text extraction\")\n\ntry:\n    from docx import Document as DocxDoc\n    HAS_DOCX = True\nexcept:\n    HAS_DOCX = False\n    print(\"WARN: python-docx not installed\")\n\n# Entity extraction patterns\nENTITY_PATTERNS = [\n    (r'(?:vendor|contractor|awarded to|awardee)[:\\s]+([A-Z][A-Za-z\\s&.,\\'\\-]+?)(?:\\.|,|\\n|$)', 'vendor_name'),\n    (r'\\$[\\d,]+(?:\\.\\d{2})?', 'dollar_amount'),\n    (r'(?:RFP|RFQ|IFB|NOFA|RFO)\\s*[#:\\-]?\\s*[\\w\\-]+', 'solicitation_number'),\n    (r'(?:EIN|FEIN|Tax\\s*ID)[:\\s#]*(\\d{2}-\\d{7})', 'ein'),\n    (r'\\b[\\w.]+@[\\w.]+\\.\\w{2,}\\b', 'email'),\n    (r'\\b(\\d{3}[-.]?\\d{3}[-.]?\\d{4})\\b', 'phone'),\n]\n\ndef extract_text_from_url(url):\n    \"\"\"Download a file and extract text from it\"\"\"\n    try:\n        resp = requests.get(url, timeout=30, stream=True)\n        if resp.status_code != 200:\n            return None, f\"HTTP {resp.status_code}\"\n        \n        content_type = resp.headers.get(\"Content-Type\", \"\")\n        data = resp.content\n        \n        text = \"\"\n        if \"pdf\" in content_type or url.lower().endswith(\".pdf\"):\n            if HAS_PDF:\n                with pdfplumber.open(io.BytesIO(data)) as pdf:\n                    for page in pdf.pages:\n                        t = page.extract_text()\n                        if t:\n                            text += t + \"\\n\"\n            else:\n                text = data.decode(\"utf-8\", errors=\"replace\")\n        elif \"word\" in content_type or url.lower().endswith(\".docx\"):\n            if HAS_DOCX:\n                doc = DocxDoc(io.BytesIO(data))\n                text = \"\\n\".join(p.text for p in doc.paragraphs)\n            else:\n                text = data.decode(\"utf-8\", errors=\"replace\")\n        elif url.lower().endswith((\".html\", \".htm\")):\n            text = data.decode(\"utf-8\", errors=\"replace\")\n            # Strip HTML tags\n            text = re.sub(r'\x3C[^>]+>', ' ', text)\n            text = re.sub(r'\\s+', ' ', text)\n        else:\n            text = data.decode(\"utf-8\", errors=\"replace\")\n        \n        return text, None\n    except Exception as e:\n        return None, str(e)\n\ndef extract_entities(text, project_id, file_name):\n    \"\"\"Extract named entities from text\"\"\"\n    entities = []\n    for pattern, label in ENTITY_PATTERNS:\n        for m in re.finditer(pattern, text, re.IGNORECASE):\n            val = m.group(1) if m.lastindex else m.group(0)\n            val = val.strip()\n            if len(val) > 2:\n                entities.append({\n                    \"project_numeric_id\": project_id,\n                    \"file_name\": file_name,\n                    \"entity_type\": label,\n                    \"entity_value\": val[:200],\n                })\n    return entities\n\ndef process_row(r):\n    \"\"\"Download and extract entities from a single file\"\"\"\n    pid = r[\"project_numeric_id\"]\n    fn = r[\"file_name\"]\n    url = r[\"download_url\"]\n    \n    text, error = extract_text_from_url(url)\n    if error:\n        return {\"project_numeric_id\": pid, \"file_name\": fn, \"status\": \"error\", \"error\": error, \"entities\": []}\n    \n    entities = extract_entities(text, pid, fn)\n    return {\n        \"project_numeric_id\": pid,\n        \"file_name\": fn,\n        \"status\": \"ok\",\n        \"text_length\": len(text),\n        \"entities\": entities,\n        \"text_preview\": text[:500],\n    }\n\nprint(f\"\\nStarting batch download of {len(signed)} signed files...\")\nresults = []\ntotal_entities = 0\ntotal_ok = 0\ntotal_err = 0\n\nwith ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=4) as pool:\n    futures = {pool.submit(process_row, r): r for r in signed}\n    done = 0\n    for f in as_completed(futures):\n        done += 1\n        res = f.result()\n        results.append(res)\n        if res[\"status\"] == \"ok\":\n            total_ok += 1\n            total_entities += entities={total_entities}\")\n\n# Save extracted entities\nout_entities = []\nfor r in results:\n    out_entities.extend(r[\"entities\"])\n\nout_path_entities = WORK_DIR / \"oc_procurement_extracted_entities.json\"\nwith open(out_path_entities, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as f:\n    json.dump(out_entities, f, indent=2, default=str)\n\nprint(f\"\\nDONE: {len(results)}) processed, {total_ok} ok, {total_err} err\")\nprint(f\"Extracted {len(out_entities)} entities\")\nprint(f\"Saved: {out_path_entities}\")\n\n# Also save text previews for BQ loading\nout_path_text = \"text_preview\": r.get(\"text_preview\", \"\"),\n    \"text_length\": r.get(\"text_length\", 0),\n} for r in results if r[\"status\"] == \"ok\"]\nwith open(out_path_text, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\")
